title: The Loose Cover
premise: Mirabel Iversen, a whistle-blower who has survived by shedding identities, takes one last anonymous case: a voiceprint that unlocks a server in Lagos and reveals a coordinated industrial 'accident' scheduled to kill hundreds while erasing evidence of corporate crimes. As Mirabel digs, they discover the attack's architect is the person who trained them to disappear—and that their own buried past is the loose thread threatening to unravel everything. Hunted across three countries by both the conspirators and the agency they once betrayed, Mirabel must choose between staying invisible and going on record as themselves. In the end, Mirabel stops the attack but deliberately surrenders their anonymity, testifying under their true name and accepting arrest, because survival without a self is just another way of disappearing.
about_author: C. M. Oyelaran is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent six years documenting supply-chain fraud before leaving the industry entirely. They write thrillers about people whose names are worth more dead than alive, and live somewhere they refuse to specify.

chapters.title: Four Names Deep
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Living in Rotterdam as 'Ingrid Voss,' Mirabel takes an unattributable case from a broker: analyze a voiceprint file for authenticity. The routine job pays well and asks no questions—exactly what Mirabel needs. Emotional beat: the brittle comfort of a life built to leave no fingerprints.

chapters.title: The Voice That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Forensic analysis reveals the voiceprint belongs to Dr. Adaeze Okonkwo—a whistleblower officially dead for two years. The recording contains coordinates and a date eleven days out. Emotional beat: recognition curdling into dread; Mirabel knows fake deaths, having arranged their own.

chapters.title: Server Room, Lagos
chapters.summary: POV: Adaeze (flashback interwoven). Two years earlier, Adaeze hid evidence of Halcyon Materials' toxic waste practices on an offshore server keyed to her voiceprint, then faked her death. Present-day Mirabel realizes unlocking the server will broadcast their location. Emotional beat: inheritance of another woman's courage.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Mirabel accesses the server remotely; within hours, someone tries to breach their safehouse network. They burn the 'Voss' identity and move. A message arrives: 'We know what you unlocked. Walk away or become part of the accident.' Emotional beat: the old reflexes firing, and failing.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas Reyes, the case broker. Reyes reveals he was paid to route this case specifically to Mirabel—someone wanted them found. He gives Mirabel a name before his shop burns down around him. Emotional beat: guilt; Mirabel's invisibility has always cost other people.

chapters.title: Halcyon Days
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Digging into Halcyon Materials, Mirabel finds the scheduled event: a refinery 'gas leak' in Port Harcourt timed to destroy records and witnesses—including Adaeze's surviving sister. Eleven days becomes ten. Emotional beat: cold fury at murder dressed as misfortune.

chapters.title: What the Training Taught
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The tradecraft signatures in the surveillance tailing Mirabel match Wren Calloway—the handler who taught Mirabel to vanish, now apparently working for Halcyon's security arm. Flashback to the day Mirabel fled the agency. Emotional beat: betrayal layered on betrayal.

chapters.title: Sister of the Dead
chapters.summary: POV: Ngozi Okonkwo. In Port Harcourt, Ngozi refuses to flee despite warnings, determined to finish her sister's work. Mirabel contacts her under yet another name. Emotional beat: two survivors circling each other, neither willing to be the first to trust.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Three Borders
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Mirabel travels to Lagos using forged credentials, evading Calloway's watchers at every checkpoint. They recover Adaeze's hidden notebook from a contact who dies of 'food poisoning' days later. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into methodical resolve.

chapters.title: The Notebook
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Adaeze's notebook maps the conspiracy: not just Halcyon, but regulators and officials paid to look away, plus a second target site Mirabel hadn't known about. The attack isn't containment—it's expansion. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of realizing the crime is bigger than the crime.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: POV: Calloway. Wren Calloway reflects on finding Mirabel—not to kill them, but because Halcyon fears what Mirabel knows about the agency's own complicity. She leaves a dead-drop message offering Mirabel a way back inside. Emotional beat: a mentor's twisted love, weaponized.

chapters.title: Old Ghosts, New Names
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Mirabel meets Calloway in a neutral café. Calloway offers protection and a new identity in exchange for silence about the agency's role. Mirabel pretends to consider. Emotional beat: performing trust while cataloguing exits—the loneliest skill they own.

chapters.title: Seven Days Out
chapters.summary: POV: Ngozi. Ngozi documents conditions at the refinery, gathering witness statements from workers who don't know they're marked. She notices Mirabel watching and confronts them directly. Emotional beat: raw courage meeting calculated caution—and slowly winning it over.

chapters.title: Alliance of the Unseen
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Mirabel tells Ngozi the truth—partially—and they plan together: expose the plot publicly before the 'accident,' forcing Halcyon to abort rather than proceed under scrutiny. They need press, proof, and timing. Emotional beat: the first real alliance Mirabel has risked in years.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Their secure channel leaks; Calloway's team raids the safehouse minutes after they leave. Ngozi is taken. Mirabel realizes the leak came from their own carelessness—an old habit, a real name half-spoken. Emotional beat: self-loathing and terror fused.

chapters.title: Four Days, One Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. To find Ngozi, Mirabel must use the identity they swore never to reuse—their original name, still flagged in agency databases. Using it lights up every screen on three continents. Emotional beat: burning the last bridge to invisibility, knowingly.

chapters.title: The Detention Block
chapters.summary: POV: Ngozi. Held in a Halcyon-controlled facility slated to be inside the blast radius, Ngozi organizes fellow detainees, memorizing guard rotations. She refuses to sign a false confession implicating Adaeze as a saboteur. Emotional beat: dignity as resistance.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Mirabel infiltrates the facility during a shift change, guided by Ngozi's smuggled notes. They extract her amid chaos, but Mirabel is shot and identified on camera—as their original self. Emotional beat: pain accepted as the price of being someone again.

chapters.title: Going Loud
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Instead of running, Mirabel broadcasts everything—server data, notebook scans, the confession Ngozi wouldn't sign—to journalists and regulators worldwide, naming themselves on record. Halcyon must abort the staged accident to avoid scrutiny. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: Calloway's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: POV: Calloway. Ordered to eliminate Mirabel quietly, Calloway instead confronts them one final time—and lets them go, unable to kill the student who finally stopped hiding. She deletes her own files and walks into the sea fog. Emotional beat: mourning the person she might have been.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Weeks later, Mirabel testifies before an international commission under their true name, flanked by Ngozi. Halcyon executives are indicted; the refinery workers are evacuated and compensated. Mirabel awaits trial for their own past crimes. Emotional beat: accountability chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. In a holding cell, Mirabel writes letters—to Reyes's family, to Adaeze's memory, to no one. Ngozi visits with news: the sentence will be short, and there's work afterward for people who know how systems break. Emotional beat: quiet peace; survival finally has a shape worth keeping.
